chapter: Small groups, Europe and Kansas City memories (repeated passages)
title: Thamon Hayes's band and Jesse Stone's Idaho
summary: Thamon Hayes's band had good arrangements by Jesse Stone, who wrote Idaho, which Bird and others played.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: It would be nice. I wouldn't be working. Because times were kind of slim in them days, you know.
But we had a great band at that time, Thamon Hayes' band.
He was a trombone player also?

Yes. We had good arrangements...good arrangements of Jesse Stone. He really could make some arrangements. You know, he's the one that wrote "Idaho" -- that's his number. And I think he's got several other numbers. But "Idaho" is one that became very famous, you know. All the guys used to play that. All the Modern guys used to play that tune....
It's funny... That's a nice tune. Nobody plays it any more.
It's kind of fallen by the wayside. It's strange.
Yeah. Bird and all them used to play that. That was one of their numbers. [SINGS THEME]
